Subject: Follow-up: Expected Monthly Tokens, Budget Range & Peak TPS (Hosted API)

Hi Ari — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap of the operational numbers we captured and a few asks so we can get you a formal hosted pricing estimate: 

Summary of traffic you described (please confirm):
- Baseline monthly tokens (conservative): ~120,000,000 tokens/month
- Expected steady-state monthly tokens: ~220,000,000 tokens/month
- Launch/peak month (marketing spike): up to ~420,000,000 tokens
- Average end-to-end tokens per API call (prompt + completion): ~900 tokens
- Peak TPS: sustained ~85 TPS during 10–15 minute windows; burst up to ~250 TPS for 30–60s
- Estimated concurrent active sessions during peak: ~180–220

A few asks so we give a clean quote:
1) Can you confirm the baseline/steady-state/peak numbers above? If ranges are better, please provide min/likely/max.
2) What is the target $/1M tokens you had in mind for a committed slab? (You referenced a ballpark during the call; please confirm.)
3) Any hard constraints on monthly spend or payment terms we should be aware of?

Attached: Lumen_traffic_snapshot_Q1.csv (rough sample you shared on the call) — helped us estimate the burst shape.

Next steps we propose: once you confirm numbers & target $/1M, we’ll run two pricing scenarios (self-serve hosted commit + burst buffer) and a Dedicated-capacity alternative if predictability is critical. Can we schedule a 30-min pricing deep-dive next week (I’m available Tue/Wed afternoon PT)?

Thanks — Tessa

--

Tessa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming / refining:
- Baseline: 120M/mo (minimum we expect after GA)
- Typical steady-state (Q3 onward): 200–240M/mo (we’re modeling 220M as the likely case)
- Peak launch month: could spike to ~400–450M (heavy marketing + initial onboarding)

Tessa / Karthik — adding quick pricing context so we’re aligned for tomorrow’s deep-dive.

Pricing scenarios (illustrative at $18 / 1M tokens):
- Scenario A (committed hosted slab): 220M tokens/mo * $18/1M = $3,960/month (billing in 1M token increments)
- Scenario B (peak month 420M): 420 * $18 = $7,560 for that month — recommend a burst buffer or short-term top-up to avoid throttles
- Scenario C (launch month 450M): 450 * $18 = $8,100 — for predictable launches we usually recommend a 1–3 month overage credit or short-term reserved uplift

Operational notes: peak TPS is the gating factor for latency/SLOs. For 250 TPS bursts at ~1k tokens per call, we need to account for concurrency and KV-cache hit rates — depending on their cache profile we can reduce GPU time per token by ~20–40%. That will affect unit economics and may allow a lower effective $/1M.

Karthik — can you bring a sketch of the burst buffer mechanics + a small cost sensitivity table that maps $/1M at 15/18/22 to monthly invoice for 120/220/420M? I’ll include a short note about contractual minimums and overage policy for Ari’s procurement contact.

Marissa
